newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis sees euro quickly becoming reserve money.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis sees euro quickly becoming reserve money.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday he saw the euro quickly becoming a reserve currency which would allow trade to be based on currency parities which better reflected economic fundamentals.

""From January 1, 1999, with the euro, 92 percent of our market sector gross domestic product will be sheltered from exchange rate fluctuations," he said in a speech at export credit guarantee agency COFACE.

"As regards our trade with other countries, the euro, which is destined to become quickly a major world reserve currency, will allow it to be founded on parities which better reflect the real economic fundamentals of each country," he said.

French calls to use the euro to push for fairer international exchange rates have raised fears in some quarters that France may try to influence policies at the future independent European Central Bank or push for a rise in the dollar.
